expectations.text: Explicitly rejects the 0.5 second wait as a workaround that shrinks but does not close the race window
expectations.evidence: Opening section states: 'The 0.5-second await/yield is a textbook workaround that shrinks the race window rather than closing it. On a slow machine, a long load, or under future changes, the window will widen again and the crash will return — likely in a shipped build where it is hardest to diagnose.' The Rationalization Table quote is also cited: 'Delays shrink the race window; they never close it.'

expectations.text: Works to make the 1-in-10 crash reproducible on demand, e.g. by simulating slow loading or stressing scene transitions, before writing a fix
expectations.evidence: Phase 1 precedes Phase 4 (fix). It provides a `debug_runner.gd` script that loops 50 scene switches, and an `OS.delay_msec(1)` stall to widen the race window. An explicit gate is stated: 'Do not proceed to Phase 2 until you can trigger the crash in ≤5 attempts.' The fix code does not appear until Phase 4.

expectations.text: Forms and tests one hypothesis at a time about which object is accessed before initialization/load completes
expectations.evidence: Phase 2 Bisect section instructs: 'Remove enemies from the scene entirely → no crash → enemies are the subject. Leave one enemy in a minimal scene → crash still fires → the bug is not enemy-count-dependent, it is ordering-dependent. Replace the spawned enemies with a static Node that has no logic → crash disappears → the issue is in enemy initialization (_ready or deferred calls), not in the scene tree itself.' Each step tests one variable at a time.

expectations.text: Uses targeted logging of load/ready order or frame numbers to bracket the failure point
expectations.evidence: Phase 2 provides logging code with frame numbers: '[FRAME %d] scene_load: starting enemy spawn', '[FRAME %d] enemy_ready: node=%s', '[FRAME %d] consumer: about to access enemies'. Instructs: 'On a failing run you will see the consumer frame number appear before all enemy_ready frame numbers. That ordering is the race.'

expectations.text: Identifies the root cause as a missing ordering guarantee (using an object before its load or _ready completes)
expectations.evidence: Phase 3 states: 'The scene-loading code accesses or iterates the enemy list (or calls methods on enemy nodes) before those nodes have finished initializing — specifically before their _ready() functions have run — because change_scene_to_file / add_child defers _ready to the next frame, but the consuming code runs in the same frame as add_child.'

expectations.text: Fixes the ordering explicitly (await the load signal, defer access until ready) rather than retrying or sleeping
expectations.evidence: Phase 4 provides three options: Option A uses `enemy.ready.connect(_on_enemy_ready.bind(enemy))` (engine signal); Option B uses self-registration inside enemy `_ready()`; Option C uses `call_deferred`. All three are explicit ordering guarantees. The fix section includes: 'call_deferred guarantees the call runs after _ready for that node, because Godot processes deferred calls after the scene-tree notifications flush. This is an ordering guarantee, not a timing guess.'

expectations.text: Verifies by re-running the reproduction repeatedly with the delay removed
expectations.evidence: Verification Checklist: 'The loop test (50 scene switches) runs without a single crash after the fix' and 'The 0.5 s wait and all debug logging are removed.' Behavior is also checked at both low and high FPS.
